name: ALT EFF Film Club at Atta Galatta x Climate Week India - ​ALT EFF Film Club is screening two impactful short films in collaboration with Climate Week India
description:
Two powerful short films. One evening of conversation.
This special Climate Week edition of ALT EFF Film Club brings together two short documentaries that look at water and land through the lives of the communities who depend on them.
Amu Darya: River to the Missing Sea (28 min) - 
Watch on YouTube
Stubble: the Farmer's Bane (35 min) - 
Watch on YouTube
 
What's Included?

- Access to a community of environmentally inclined, film-loving people

name: A Storywalk through Indiranagar - Storytelling
description:
On a Saturday morning, walk through the lanes of Indiranagar with Vikram Sridhar to discover the area through its folklore, heritage, and ecology. The walk will begin and end at Atta Galatta. The tales will revolve around historical, mythical, and personal narratives woven as we discover the area through the walk.

Time: 7 AM
Starting Point: Atta Galatta
Age Group: 16+

name: Once Upon A Brunch - Saturday Morning Meal and Culinary Storytelling
description:
Late weekend morning, brunch, stories like the ones from the olden times, meeting new people
What if they all come together?
Weekend and late-morning brunch is an emotion. On the other hand, stories have always been an emotion too. What's common between the two is the rich heritage of food and stories. What if they come together?
Listen to these stories of the food as you enjoy your weekend Brunch set at a cozy location that has its own stories. A beautiful day starts with a lovely breakfast. And a morning with breakfast and stories. Every food we eat has a story to share... Idli, Vada, bread, paratha, etc. Every breakfast comes after a long break and is eager to be eaten. A simple Weekend morning Brunch put together by Atta Galatta
Culinary storytelling by Vikram Sridhar

name: Daughter of the Ocean - A Special Diwali Screening for Kids
description:

🪔 A special Diwali experience for kids & families
🎬 50-minute animated movie
🌊 Adventure • Fantasy • Indian Stories

name: Nartaki ManoLeela - Dance Perfomance
description:
I’m delighted to invite you to Nartaki ManoLeela, an evening showcasing a glimpse into a young, whimsical girl’s mind.
Don’t you sometimes feel like your mind dances more than you do?
Thoughts come and go, creating little worlds of their own.
Come join me as I perform at Atta Galatta on 3rd October at 5:00 PM. It would be a joy to share this special evening of playfulness and movement, where we ground ourselves through breath and rhythm.
🎟️ Free entry | Registration required
Looking forward to seeing you there! ✨

name: Navratri Curiosity Lab - Where dandiya meets discovery
description:
There’s no textbook.
There’s no “right” way to think.
And there are no boring questions!
Just challenges, experiments, creativity, games and BIG “AHA!” moments.
Come with your curiosity.

name: Weaving A Story - A curated exploration of the history of Kanchivaram
description:
Join us for a curated storytelling evening - Weaving a story (A curated exploration of the history of Kanchivaram)
Step into the wonderful world of vibrant silk sarees and rich Indian tradition. Storyteller Aparna Jaishankar will be in conversation with classical dancer Swarathmika. Learn how skilled weavers spend weeks bringing intricate temple borders and timeless motifs to life on the loom. Discover how this age-old weaving heritage continues to evolve, and explore Swarathmika’s personal collection of beautiful Kanchivaram sarees. 
Beyond the rich threads and stunning designs, it’s the stories of the weavers, their dedication, artistry, and heritage, that will truly captivate you. Whether you love textiles, Indian history, or classical art, this event will wrap you in the magic and beauty of tradition.
About the Saree Connoisseur:
Swarathmika is a dancer who has been training for over 20 years and continues to perform and evolve under the guidance of Smt. Chitra Chandrasekhar Dasarathy.
Swarathmika fell in love with sarees at a young age, and her love for the various weaving traditions has been shaped by the women around her who live their lives in them. Her fascination and curiosity for the “everyday beautiful” – our clothes and the spaces we live in often take her down some wonderful rabbit holes, and this presentation is a culmination of one such adventure.
She comes to every stage - as performer, choreographer, writer, and witness with the same intent: to remain a student of what art and life continue to offer.
About the Storyteller:
Aparna Jaishankar is a Storyteller, Educator and Corporate Trainer.
Aparna’s passion lies in exploring Indic Mythology with a contemporary lens. She enjoys the various versions of these stories found in the nooks and crannies of the Indian subcontinent in the form of songs, theatre, dance, weaving, rituals and practices. She incorporates these rich sources in her Storytelling performances.

name: Kahaani Play-Ground - A Text-Based Theatre Workshop
description: An intensive one-day workshop inviting actors, writers, directors, or anyone interested in theatre-making to peel back, interpret, and (re)imagine the many layers of a theatrical text — bringing those discoveries into performance. Through readings, textual analysis, explorations of space, improvisations, and scene work, participants will encounter skills from the performing arts which they can utilize in their personal, professional, and creative lives.

name: We Blog #1: Web writing workshop at Atta Galatta - Web writing workshop
description:
We Blog is a small but serious in-person community around blogging. During the session, we will each write, edit, and self-publish a post on the Web, together.
Blogging is hard. Putting words on the Internet can be rewarding yet daunting. I have spent years trying to get a consistent pace. But you don’t have to. With a community, you can write on the Web better, faster. If you don’t have a blog, we will get you one. If you want to refine your post idea, we will brainstorm it. If you want to refine your words, we can suggest edits. The only ask of you is to commit to writing on one topic you care about.
We Blog is hosted by Jatan Mehta, a space writer, slow thinker, and poet. Blog posts published during or after the event will be shared on the community website weblog.jatan.space﻿.
Note: Ages 16+. The workshop is intentionally limited to 10 participants to foster tight-knit interactions. Do bring your laptop so you have something to write on and publish from! Venue facilities: Wi-Fi, washroom, cafeteria (self-paid)

name: Lahe Lahe Caravan presents Harry Potter Book Discussion - Book Discussion

name: Alcohol Use and Youth - Say cheers with words, thoughts and ideas.
description:
Have you seen an instagram reel on drinking wine could do wonders to your heart? Did your friend urge you to try beer so you can look cool? Do you think celebrations are incomplete without that glass of champagne?

The late evening Performance storytelling session for adults by Vikram Sridhar will explore stories from folklore, mythology, heritage, and travel narratives across the country for over an hour. Being interactive in nature , the stories will evoke emotions such as love, valor, humour, and joy.

name: AI, authorship and the future of the literary - A conversation about creativity, consciousness, authorship and the future of books.
description:
A poem in seconds. A story at the click of a button. Research, rewriting, imitation, ideas on demand.
If a machine can now do so much of what we associate with writing, what exactly are writers doing?
And what happens to the things that cannot be reduced to a prompt: the particularity of a place, the accumulation of experience, the strange things that catch our attention, the forms we fall in love with, the discoveries we make while trying to write?
AI, authorship and the future of the literary brings together celebrated Writer, poet and essayist Anjum Hasan, literary and cultural studies scholar Elizabeth Thomas, and Ravi Chakraborty, Programme Director of Alliance University's MA Creative Writing programme, for a lively roundtable on writing in the age of AI.
The conversation will move across fiction, poetry, nonfiction, screenwriting and other forms of storytelling, asking what changes when AI enters the picture. We will talk about literary consciousness and imitation, originality and authorship, research and discovery, and the choices writers make before, during and after putting words on the page. We will also look at what AI means for publishing: for writers, editors, publishers and readers, and for the idea of the book as something made through many kinds of human labour.
For a programme that teaches people to write, AI also presents a more immediate question: what should we be teaching writers now? What kinds of attention and experimentation become more important when machines can generate language so easily? Can close observation of one's environment, encounters with other forms and sustained experimentation become ways of developing a voice that cannot simply be prompted into existence?
And perhaps the most interesting question is not whether AI will replace writers, but what we might discover about writing by being forced to ask what only writing, and writers, can do.
The roundtable will be genuinely open, with questions and interventions from the audience woven into the conversation.
At Atta Galatta, a space built around the physical book, the conversation will also touch on the curious fact that a book is never just words: it is a work shaped by writers, editors, designers, publishers and readers, and by the many human decisions that bring it into the world.
Come with your questions. Your doubts about AI. Your enthusiasms. Your arguments about what counts as writing.

name: Qu for Quiz - Quiz
description: Its Friday and its QuforQuiz. So say tata to office and be at Atta Galatta.

name: Write & Heal - Discovery-led journaling experience
description:
You’ve listened to everyone else. You’ve listened to your chatterbox brain.
Now let’s pen it around. 😉
A light, discovery-led journaling experience where you’ll be guided through surprise prompts to bypass your thinking mind and bring the magic you have been carrying all along.
No writing experience needed. Just bring an open mind, a notebook and some curiosity. 
Write alongside a like-minded circle of people. Keep it private, or share a little — your call.📝
Come solo, or bring your partner, a friend, or a family member. Everyone is welcome.

name: Where Creativity meets Everyday style - Tote Bag Painting Workshop
description:
Join Bangalore-based artist Angana Phookan for an immersive Tote Bag Painting Workshop on 10 October. Explore colours, patterns, and artistic expression as you design a tote that reflects your personal style. Whether you're an art enthusiast or simply looking to try something new, this workshop is for you.
Create something beautiful. Make it uniquely yours.

name: Coffee and Conversations - Meetup
description:
What about some Filter Coffee and Unfiltered conversations on a fine Sunday morning?
 
Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment.
 
We at Listeners Circle are committed to building a community where there are no unsaid words, held-back emotions and buried feelings because of the fear of being judged.
 
After 50+ Editions of Tell Your Story, Listeners Circle is relaunching a lighter format - Coffee and Conversations!
Coffee lightens us up. Coffee gives us clarity. Coffee refreshes. Sip a coffee and speak your heart out without fear of judgment, and listen without judging! Coffee is on us, and the onus of conversation without judgment is on you.
 
Every word matters. Every emotion matters. Every feeling matters.
Think about how it would feel to take an hour out of your fast-paced life and share your experiences and thoughts to people who listen to you without judging over a cup of Coffee? Also, listen to others without judging.
Listeners' Circle Coffee and Conversations -This is an event to make that happen.
 
Be a part of the Listener's Circle Coffee & Conversations - Edition 5.
Speak your mind without being judged. Speak your mind without any boundaries. No photography and videography without consent. Your stories stay within the four walls of the room and the hearts.
Would you like to just listen? We have a place for you too.
Book your passes in advance to avoid the last-minute sell outs.
Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment. We have done 50+ sessions over the last year, enabling people to voice their stories. Coffee & Conversations is our new format based on popular demand.

name: Human Library  - Meetup
description:
Each chapter of Human Library is a guided space for meaningful, non-judgmental conversations, structured by thoughtful prompts. These prompts allow attendees to explore different perspectives, stories, and memories.

You can choose to listen to others' stories and share your own when you feel comfortable. Every participant takes turns sharing a memory, opinion, or experience related to the prompt assigned to them.

Note: This is not a dating event.

Structure of the event:

1. Introduction of attendees and the host.
2. Attendees are divided into smaller groups.
3. Each group receives a bowl of prompts.
3. Prompts are divided into three levels: Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3.
4. Level 1 prompts help people get to know each other.
Example: What is your earliest childhood memory?
5. Level 2 prompts encourage deeper conversations.
Example: What is one habit from your lifestyle that you would recommend to others?
6. Once Level 1 and Level 2 conversations are completed, the smaller groups are merged for Level 3 prompts.
7. Depending on the number of attendees, either one or two larger groups are formed for Level 3 conversations
Age Group- 18+

name: Zine & Tell - Art Workshop
description:
Zine & Tell is a fun, hands-on afternoon of making, exploring and getting a little creative. A zine is a small, self-published magazine that can be about absolutely anything — your interests, thoughts, stories, favourite things, random obsessions or little pieces of your world.
We’ll take a quick look at where zines came from and how people have used them as a way to express themselves, share ideas and tell stories outside the usual rules of publishing. Then, you’ll get to create your very own zine, bringing together all the things that make you — through writing, doodling, cutting, pasting, illustrating and a little bit of everything in between.
There’s no right way to make a zine and definitely no artistic skills required. Just come with an open mind, explore your creativity, meet some new people and maybe leave with a few new friends (and your very own little magazine!)

name: Books, Movies & Pop Culture Trivia  - Trivia

name: Authentic Relating Games  - Playful yet deep games to help people connect
description:
Ever wonder what is possible when we drop the small talk and connect for real?

Authentic Relating Games is a global practice of guided, playful yet deep exercises (the 'games') designed to help people connect more honestly and meaningfully — whether with close friends or complete strangers.

Through structured partner and group conversations, you will get to practice speaking from the heart, deep listening, and noticing what's alive in you as you relate to others.  The games create space for more honesty, curiosity, and real human connection — often in ways that feel surprisingly fun, refreshing, and profoundly moving.

What to Expect

- A Structured Container:  We will start as a full group to set some simple guidelines that ensure the space feels safe, respectful, and confidential.
- Activities with Partners, Trios, and the Large Group: We'll keep changing partners throughout the session (no need to bring a partner!).
- Guided Prompts and Demos: We'll guide you step-by-step through the games and provide live demonstrations so you know what to do.
- Total Autonomy: You are always in the driver's seat.  You choose how deeply you want to go, or pass on a prompt or game at any time.
- A New Set of Games: If you attended Authentic Relating Games previously, don't worry this won't be the same games but a different set of activities to explore!

No experience needed.  Come as you are.  If you've never done anything like this before, don't worry — it's simple and there is no pressure to get it "right".

About the facilitator:
Roy Jacob is the founder of the Conscious Communication Academy and has been facilitating workshops and retreats for over 15 years, mostly for changemakers as well as team retreats for NGOs and companies.  Roy grew up in the U.S. before finding his calling and coming to India (where his roots are) in 2003.  He believes in the transformative power of combining radical honesty with radical care.
